samples.summary: Docs picker's hover prefetch queries `document.fonts.check()` while a preview subset for that family is still connected — a path the new release never covers
samples.evidence: `onPrefetch={ensureFont}` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:449, also :646 and the third picker ~:712) runs while the dropdown list is OPEN, i.e. exactly when the row's `&text=` subset link is connected (font-family-picker.tsx:150 injects it on scroll-in). `ensureFont` (docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:345-355) forwards to `FontRegistry.ensureFont`, whose first act is `document.fonts.check(fontSpec)` (packages/docs/src/view/fonts.ts:302). With the subset connected, `check()` returns true and the registry records `status = 'loaded'` permanently for that family (fonts.ts:303, a Map never invalidated), so the registry will never load the real face for it again this session. The delta's `releasePreviewFontLinks()` only runs on list unmount (font-family-picker.tsx:177) and inside `applyPick` (:198) — neither covers the hover window, so this is a reachable bypass of the new lifetime guard. Fix belongs on the docs prefetch site (await `ensureFontLink` before touching the registry) or on the registry's `check()`.

Because the delta now releases the subset before `onChange` (font-family-picker.tsx:198), the `load()` fires with NO face connected for the family, resolves instantly, and the registry latches `status='loaded'` (fonts.ts:310) against fallback metrics. Same un-awaited pattern also at packages/frontend/src/app/slides/theme-builder-panel.tsx:100.

verdict.reason: The finding's causal chain does not exist in this repo. `ensureFont` (docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:345-355) never reaches `FontRegistry.ensureFont`: it calls `ensureFontLink(family)` and then `store.fonts?.ensureFont?.(family)`, an optional-chained call on a field no DocStore has. The `DocStore` interface (packages/docs/src/store/store.ts:11+) declares no `fonts` member, and neither implementation defines one — `MemDocStore` (packages/docs/src/store/memory.ts:32) and `YorkieDocStore` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:549) both return zero grep hits for `fonts`. The toolbar comment at :342-344 says so outright. Repo-wide, `new FontRegistry` appears only in packages/docs/test/view/fonts.test.ts:63, so no registry instance exists at runtime, and `document.fonts.check()` at packages/docs/src/view/fonts.ts:302 — the sole `check()` call in any `packages/**/src` file — is never invoked from the hover path. The permanent `status='loaded'` poisoning the finding describes therefore cannot happen. Secondary inaccuracies: the "third picker ~:712" (docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:709-712) passes no `onPrefetch` at all, and the live effect of hover, `ensureFontLink`, actively *removes* the family's preview subset once its full stylesheet settles (font-catalog.ts:192-199) rather than querying the Font Loading API against it.

verdict.reason: The finding's harm chain requires the un-awaited `ensureFontLink` to be followed by a Font Loading API query; neither cited site does that. Docs: `docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:350` drops the promise, but the next line's hop `store.fonts?.ensureFont?.(family)` (:354) is a permanently-undefined stub — `DocStore` (packages/docs/src/store/store.ts:11) has no `fonts` member (zero `fonts` matches in packages/docs/src/store), `YorkieDocStore` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:549) has none either, `FontRegistry` is never instantiated outside packages/docs/test/view/fonts.test.ts:63, and no `.fonts =` assignment exists anywhere under packages/**/*.{ts,tsx}. So `document.fonts.check()`/`load()` and the `status='loaded'` latch at packages/docs/src/view/fonts.ts:302-310 are unreachable from this path; the toolbar's own comment at :342-344 documents the stub. Slides: `theme-builder-panel.tsx:100` calls `ensureFontLink` then `store.updateTheme` with no Font Loading API call after it. Both editors recover correct metrics via `document.fonts` events instead — packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2668-2692 (loadingdone + fonts.ready → clearMeasureCache/invalidateLayout/render) and packages/slides/src/view/editor/editor.ts:1062-1069 (loadingdone → clearMeasureCache + repaint) — which fire when the real face arrives regardless of promise awaiting. The rule at font-catalog.ts:156 is conditional on calling load()/check(), and the two genuine querying callers (apply-font-family.ts:39-41, pdf-actions.ts:47-59) both await. The described defect is not present as claimed.

finding.summary: `releasePreviewFontLinks` removes faces with no relayout/repaint notification, so docs and slides keep measurements/pixels derived from the deleted subset face
finding.evidence: Both canvas editors invalidate their measure caches only on font *arrival*: `document.fonts` `loadingdone` in packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2676 (`clearMeasureCache(); invalidateLayout(); render()`) and packages/slides/src/view/editor/editor.ts:1063. Injecting a subset for a family the open document actually uses fires `loadingdone` and relayouts the document behind the menu against the subset metrics; the new `releasePreviewFontLinks()` (font-catalog.ts:246-253) then removes those faces silently — removal fires no font event — so the docs measure cache and the dirty-gated slides canvas keep the subset-derived layout/raster until some unrelated edit or font load. verdict.reason: The absence is real. `releasePreviewFontLinks()` (font-catalog.ts:246-253) and `removePreviewFontLink()` (font-catalog.ts:224-226) only call `link.remove()`; there is no event, callback, or exported notification. Both canvas consumers invalidate exclusively on font *arrival*: docs at editor.ts:2668-2692 (`loadingdone` -> clearMeasureCache/invalidateLayout/render, plus a mount-only `fonts.ready` fallback) and slides at editor/editor.ts:1062-1069 (`loadingdone` -> clearMeasureCache/markDirty/render). Face removal fires neither event, and docs' measure cache is drained ONLY by that handler (editor.ts:2672) — the ~20 `invalidateLayout()` call sites drop the layout cache but keep subset-derived widths, so staleness persists past ordinary edits. I searched for any release-side notification and found none: no `dispatchEvent`/`CustomEvent`/`MutationObserver` in packages/{frontend,docs,slides}/src, and both callers (font-family-picker.tsx:175-178, :198; more-fonts-dialog.tsx:174-177) invoke it bare. I also tested the premise's reachability rather than assuming it: `ensurePreviewFontLink` skips families with a full link (hasFullFamilyLink, font-catalog.ts:289-308), but no document-open preload exists — every `ensureFontLink` call site is pick/hover/export driven (docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:350, apply-font-family.ts:35, text-edit-section.tsx:68, mobile-toolbar.tsx:554, pdf-actions.ts:48) and useGoogleFontsLink injects only the 8 `eager` families, so a document painting a non-eager web family genuinely has no full link and its picker row will inject a subset. The pick path self-heals only incidentally (the picked family's own ensureFontLink load re-fires `loadingdone`); the close-without-pick path leaves the docs measure cache and the dirty-gated slides raster pinned to the deleted subset face. This is a cross-package invariant violation of the kind this lens covers: the shared frontend module now removes faces that other packages' caches assumed only ever get added.

finding.summary: Slides family-apply calls `document.fonts.load` immediately after the now-async `ensureFontLink`, so it can resolve against the subset preview face and repaint the dirty-gated canvas exactly once, with the wrong glyphs
finding.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/slides/toolbar/apply-font-family.ts:28-39: `ensureFontLink(family);` (promise dropped) then `document.fonts.load(`16px ${JSON.stringify(family)}`).then(() => { editor.markDirty(); editor.render(); })`. Since this change, the family the user just picked normally already has a `&text=` subset link in the head (injected by the picker's in-view observer, packages/frontend/src/components/text-formatting/font-family-picker.tsx:149), and a subset face has no `unicode-range`, so `load()` resolves instantly against it. The single `markDirty`/`render` then fires against the label-only face; because the slides renderer is dirty-gated (see the comment at apply-font-family.ts:17-21), nothing repaints when the real family finally arrives — the canvas keeps the wrong glyphs until an unrelated edit. Both slides toolbars route through this helper (text-edit-section.tsx:65ff, mobile-toolbar.tsx:549ff). The fix is to await the returned promise, as `pdf-actions.ts` now does.

verdict.reason: The finding claims `applySlideFontFamily` drops `ensureFontLink`'s promise and calls `document.fonts.load` immediately, so the single dirty-gated repaint can resolve against the picker's `&text=` subset face. The actual code does the opposite: apply-font-family.ts:35 captures the promise (`const linked = ensureFontLink(family);`) and lines 39-44 chain `linked.then(() => document.fonts.load(...)).then(() => { editor.markDirty(); editor.render(); })` — i.e. it already awaits the stylesheet wait, the exact fix the finding prescribes and the same shape as pdf-actions.ts:48. The file's header comment (apply-font-family.ts:23-28) documents this ordering as load-bearing. Supporting: ensureFontLink (font-catalog.ts:174-203) resolves on the full link's load/error and removes the preview link in its own `.then` (font-catalog.ts:192-199), and findFontLink (font-catalog.ts:124-132) matches only `data-wafflebase-font`, never `data-wafflebase-font-preview`, so a subset link cannot short-circuit the returned promise either. Both toolbars cited (text-edit-section.tsx:68, mobile-toolbar.tsx:554) route through this same helper, so no alternate un-awaited path exists for slides family apply.
